In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of the AV1451 positron emission tomography tracer is an important and useful adjunct to the diagnosis of Alzheimer disease, but it is not yet sufficiently sensitive or specific to serve as a stand-alone diagnostic tool.
Alzheimer disease biomarker discrepancies between CSF phosphorylated tau (181P and 217P) and AV1451 PET are not uncommon.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
AV1451 PET is a useful tool for the diagnosis of dementia and for monitoring disease progression.
we have identified a group of individuals who have high levels of phosphorylated tau in the CSF but do not have the expected amount of amyloid plaques on PET imaging.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of CSF phosphorylated tau (p-tau) and AV1451 PET is more accurate in detecting AD pathology than either test alone.
